findings.bug: The @param javadoc extraction regex has no word boundary after the parameter name, so a record component whose name is a prefix of another component's name matches the wrong @param line.
findings.why_real: The pattern String.format("(?<=@param +%s).*?...", paramName) uses a lookbehind of '@param +foo' which also matches the '@param foo' prefix inside '@param foobar'; getJavaDoc(RecordComponentElement) uses matcher.find() which returns the first match in document order, so component 'foo' can capture 'foobar's documentation. A word-boundary (\\b or a trailing separator) is required, as the sibling exact-name intent shows.
findings.how_to_prove: Build javadoc 'Some record.\n@param foobar the bar value\n@param foo real foo'; paramJavadocPattern("foo").matcher(doc).find() -> group() is 'bar the bar value' (from @param foobar) instead of the expected ' real foo'.

findings.bug: The self-reference guard 'resolved != typeVariable' only prevents a one-node cycle (A->A); a two-node mapping cycle (A->B, B->A) causes unbounded recursion and StackOverflowError.
findings.why_real: resolveGeneric recurses whenever the resolved value is a TypeVariable other than the key, but only compares against the immediate key, not the recursion chain; the class elsewhere (TypeExtractor.visitTypeVariable/hasCycle) explicitly guards against generic cycles, showing cycles are a real concern this method does not fully handle.
findings.how_to_prove: Populate a TypeDescriptor.generics map with two TypeVariables mapped to each other (A->B, B->A) and call resolveGeneric(A); expected a terminating result but actual is StackOverflowError.
